characterInteraction.description: Interviewer-interviewee dynamic. Schieffer sets the context, Graham provides his viewpoint.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Graham's strong stance on debt reduction underscores the fiscal conservatism of the Republican party.

mood.description: Pensive - Serious discussion about national debt and its impact on future generations.

narrativeProgression.description: Schieffer poses a question about responding to claims of radicalism regarding debt ceiling raises, Graham explains his stance and emphasizes the need for presidential leadership.
Graham asserts that the country is in deep debt, putting children's futures at risk.
He emphasizes the need to cut government spending.

characterInteraction.description: Interviewer-interviewee dynamic with brief back-and-forth between the senators.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Warner's emphasis on bipartisanship contrasts with Graham's criticism of Obama's administration, reflecting the partisan divide over fiscal issues.

mood.description: Hopeful, then Pensive - Warner starts with optimism about finding a solution, but Graham ends with a more cautious outlook.

narrativeProgression.description: Schieffer asks Warner about progress in the 'Gang of Six,' Warner outlines the plan's key elements and emphasizes the need for bipartisan cooperation.
Schieffer then questions Graham about the likelihood of action before the election, and Graham expresses doubt, highlighting the lack of progress during President Obama's term.
Warner mentions a bipartisan group of 45 senators seeking a solution.
Graham criticizes President Obama's budgets for receiving zero votes and Democrats for not voting on a budget since 2009.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Graham's call for boldness implies a critique of both Obama and Romney's perceived unwillingness to make tough decisions.

mood.description: Critical - Graham expresses frustration with the current political climate and lack of leadership.

narrativeProgression.description: Graham criticizes both candidates for not taking a bolder stance on debt reduction, advocating for a clear plan based on the 'Gang of Six' proposal.
Graham suggests both candidates should embrace the 'Gang of Six' plan as a roadmap for fiscal solvency.

props.name: image of the US Capitol building behind Schieffer

scenes.thematicElements: Presidential leadership, political courage, need for reform.
scenes.title: Critique of Leadership and Proposals for Reform

scenes.contextualRelevance: Warner's analysis suggests a broader systemic crisis, implying that partisan gridlock hinders the government's ability to address critical issues.

mood.description: Concerned - Warner expresses concern over the political stalemate and the lack of institutional support for necessary reforms.

narrativeProgression.description: Schieffer asks Warner about the possibility of action before the election, Warner reiterates the need for bipartisan cooperation and highlights the potential for a fiscal crisis if reforms are not implemented.
Schieffer then probes deeper into the root cause of the political gridlock.
Warner acknowledges that President Obama initially supported the 'Gang of Six' plan but failed to secure enough votes.
Warner argues that the debt and deficit issue has become a test of the functionality of American institutions.

props.name: image of the US Capitol building behind Schieffer

scenes.thematicElements: Political dysfunction, institutional failure, urgent need for action.
scenes.title: Analysis of Political Stalemate

Cut transition from Schieffer to Warner

scenes.contextualRelevance: Graham's proposal reveals a growing acceptance of tax increases among some Republicans, signifying a potential shift in party ideology.

mood.description: Resigned - Graham acknowledges the lack of progress under Obama and offers a potential solution involving tax code reforms and spending cuts.

narrativeProgression.description: Schieffer seeks Graham's analysis on the current political stalemate, prompting him to recount Obama's inaction despite Democratic majorities.
Graham outlines a potential solution emphasizing tax code changes and a shift in focus from tax cuts to debt reduction.
Graham observes that President Obama missed opportunities for reform during his first two years with strong Democratic support.
He suggests a 'breakthrough' for Republicans would involve reducing deductions and exemptions while using some of the savings for debt reduction.

climax.description: The climax is realized through Warner's and Graham's statements on the improbability of action on the proposals before the election.

storylines.description: The interview navigates through the issues of national debt and spending, focusing on proposals like the 'Gang of Six'. It highlights the challenges in achieving bipartisan cooperation and presents a critique of current political leadership.

content_metadata.title: Political Interview on Debt and Spending

youtube_description:
Senator Lindsey Graham was a guest on CBS Face the Nation Sunday, where he discussed the need to get our fiscal house in order through deficit reductions plans like Simpson-Bowles and the Gang of Six.  

Graham appeared with Senator Mark Warner (D-Virginia).
